headline: AI agent debloats Android TV for 'unbelievable' performance upgrade
summary: An AI engineer used Claude Code to optimize his smart TV, making it run smoother than when it was new, all without root access.
details: An AI engineer has successfully revitalized his Android smart TV by using Claude Code to remove unnecessary bloatware and optimize system performance. The AI agent connected via ADB, deactivated apps, installed a new launcher, and shortened animation durations, resulting in a TV that now runs smoother than it did when it was first purchased.

This optimization was achieved without requiring root access, a common hurdle for deep system modifications. The developer, Mert Cobanov, has created a website to guide others through the process, sharing the exact prompt used to instruct Claude Code.

Cobanov emphasizes that the debloating process is reversible. The AI agent keeps a log of all disabled components, allowing users to easily re-enable them if needed. Individual apps can also be restored if accidentally removed.

Sluggish performance is a common complaint with many smart TVs due to limited processing power, RAM, and storage, often exacerbated by software updates. This AI-driven solution offers an alternative to purchasing external streaming devices.

headline_marked: Microsoft [[enabling Windows 11 security feature]] that may impact gaming performance
headline: Microsoft enabling Windows 11 security feature that may impact gaming performance
summary: Windows 11's memory integrity protection is set to be enabled on more devices next month, a feature designed to stop malicious code but which may reduce gaming framerates on some hardware.
details: Microsoft is preparing to automatically enable its memory integrity security feature on more Windows 11 devices starting next month. This kernel-level protection aims to prevent malicious code or drivers from running on a system.

While memory integrity enhances security by only allowing trusted kernel-mode code and drivers to execute, Microsoft has previously cautioned that it can negatively affect PC gaming performance. The impact may be more noticeable on older processors, though modern CPUs might see less of a framerate drop.

Users who have previously disabled memory integrity will not have it automatically re-enabled by the upcoming Windows quality updates. The feature is part of Microsoft's commitment to making Windows secure by design and default, also enabling Virtualization-based Security (VBS) on eligible devices.

To check the status of memory integrity on your Windows 11 PC, you can search for 'Core Isolation' in Windows search and access the setting within the Windows Security app. If gaming performance is a priority, Microsoft suggests re-enabling memory integrity after finishing your gaming sessions.
